purpose: Required acceptance scenarios; a listed scenario is not a claim that cloud or live-source testing has passed.

scenarios.expect: New notice creates a stable notice/event ID and archives the linked official body.
An inserted old-date item is discovered by link identity rather than excluded by date watermark.
Pinned old notice does not stop traversal of new items or change the admissions year.
Changed body SHA256 creates a new version while the previous original remains.
Same attachment URL with new bytes creates a new asset version.
Retain old/new quoted deadline evidence and invalidate obsolete future alerts.
Separate application, material and preapplication nodes; unknown time is not invented.
Pagination or seed backfill records coverage bounds and unfinished cursors.
Failure is recorded explicitly and never reported as no new notices.
Body not counted complete; raw error/protection evidence retained.
Preserve requested/final URL and validate official scope before accepting new host.
Keep original bytes and distinguish OCR/date review pending from text completeness.
Fetch once but preserve all institution-to-source bindings and separate recruitment/training codes.
A parent charter does not suppress independent institute/college requirements.
Hash mismatch fails before restoration and existing destination remains intact.
Reject ../, absolute path, symlink and entries absent from the manifest.
Personal settings/raw/state/environment directories absent from staged public package.
Staging-only config binds registry/manifest SHA; original seven files are not claimed rechecked in cloud.
Restore fails except explicit first bootstrap; network/auth failure never implies empty state.
Create draft, upload, download and verify every body/asset/state byte, then publish.
Actual public-runner result per source, distinct from local GET success.
Cloud run completes while local services and machine are not needed.
One notification channel failure does not block the other; persistent attempts remain.
Persistent event ID avoids silent drop; retries may be labeled duplicates rather than claiming exactly once.
Actual device receives a push while locked; API receipt is separately recorded.
Record real run intervals, source gaps and restoration; delayed/dropped schedule is visible.
